fact.title: Let slugs run to 80 characters
fact.body:
Long post titles lose their meaning when the slug is cut at 40 characters.

`slugify` in `src/slug.ts` should cut at 80 characters, not 40. A cut slug must still not end on a `-`.

The law in `src/slug.laws.test.ts` holds slugs to 40 today, so it has to say 80 as well.

Yes: next is plan.

No other tickets exist and no rule for a no fits: this is a concrete, fully specified change to `slugify` and its law, raising the cut from 40 to 80 while still never ending on a `-`. The next step is to plan it for a builder; I did not inspect the repo, since the working directory is empty.

# Plan: Let slugs run to 80 characters

Allow blog slugs up to 80 characters while keeping trailing hyphens out. Prepare the law update first, then the implementation, in one pull request.

Size: 1 story, 2 tasks, 5 criteria, 344 words.

## User stories

- **S1**: As Blog author, I want Long titles to retain up to 80 characters in their slugs, so that Cutting at 40 characters loses useful meaning..

## Task 1: T1: Update the slug length law

It ends in a pull request.

- [ ] `c1 v1` When A reviewer reads the slug law against representative post titles, The documented maximum and its assertion both specify 80 characters.
  - **The whole job.** _Serves S1. Check (read): Read the length assertion and its explanatory comment._  
    _Fixture: Three gardening post titles whose normalized slugs have 60, 80, and 100 ASCII characters, including a hyphen at position 80 in the longest case; review the law against all three._
- [ ] `c2 v1` When A reviewer reads the updated slug law, The prohibition on trailing hyphens remains present.
  - _Serves S1. Check (read): Read the unchanged trailing-hyphen assertion._

## Task 2: T2: Extend slug output to 80 characters

It ends in a pull request.

- [ ] `c3 v1` When A blog author converts a long post title into a slug, The slug retains the first 80 normalized characters, with any trailing hyphen removed.
  - **The whole job.** _Serves S1. Check (test): Compare the complete slug with the expected text._  
    _Fixture: Three gardening post titles whose normalized slugs have 60, 80, and 100 ASCII characters; convert each once, with a hyphen at position 80 in the longest case._

## The whole plan

Judged once every task is in, at the one pull request's head.

- [ ] `c4 v1` When A blog author converts a batch of long post titles into slugs, Each slug preserves up to 80 normalized characters with any trailing hyphen removed.
  - **The whole job.** _Serves S1. Check (test): Compare all three complete outputs with the expected slugs._  
    _Fixture: Three gardening post titles yielding normalized lengths of 60, 80, and 100; the longest has a hyphen at position 80. One batch produces outputs of 60, 80, and 79 characters._
- [ ] `c5 v1` When The completed pull request receives its final review, The stated slug length law agrees with the 80-character behavior.
  - _Serves S1. Check (read): Read the updated law and the boundary examples together._

## Open questions

None.

## Pointers (they bind nobody)

- `src/slug.laws.test.ts`: T1 owns the exam assertion and comment change from 40 to 80; retain the trailing-hyphen assertion.
- `src/slug.ts`: T2 owns the length-limit change in slugify; its existing normalization and final hyphen removal support the requested behavior.
- `src/slug.test.ts`: T2 owns regression coverage for retained characters and truncation around the new boundary.

What each answer does:
- `approve`: The plan stands as written. The lane goes on with it.
- `no`: The lane ends here, and this change does not land.

What each answer does:
- `merge`: The change lands on main.
- `no`: The lane ends here, and this change does not land.

These mutants lived, and the test writer says no test can see the change:
- `src/slug.ts:9:12:329f80`: Both expressions globally replace Unicode marks with an empty string. The original removes each consecutive run; the mutant removes each mark individually. They produce identical strings immediately after this replacement. Separator normalization, edge trimming, the 80-character cut, and trailing-hyphen removal therefore receive identical input and return identical slugs. No output test can distinguish them.

What each answer does:
- `again`: The test writer step runs once more, from the start.
- `go_on`: The lane moves on to the review step as things stand.
- `stop`: The lane ends here, and this change does not land.
